answer_1.quote: The output is represented in YAML format and encodes either binary outcomes (with event counts and totals for intervention and comparator groups) or continuous outcomes (with group-wise means, standard deviations, and sample sizes). The model learns to generate these structured summaries conditioned on the corresponding textual evidence.
answer_1.outputs: Structured YAML outputs encoding numerical evidence for binary or continuous outcomes

answer_2.quote: We report a range of metrics to assess both end-to-end performance and intermediate reasoning accuracy. For the end-to-end task of predicting the final conclusion label of each study, we report accuracy and F1 score. Following Yun et al. ( ), we also evaluate the quality of numerical extraction using exact match (EM), EM@1 (at least one positional match), as well as the mean squared error (MSE) of the computed point estimate derived from the extracted values. In addition, we measure the Error Impact Rate (EIR), defined as the ratio between the number of extraction errors that lead to a flipped conclusion and the number of total extraction errors at the study level.

answer_4.quote: To this end, we manually annotate the outputs of both models on 30 biomedical studies, for which human annotators had previously identified the sources of the correct numbers (see Appendix C), assigning a single label to each reasoning process.
answer_4.guideline: Labels distinguish whether the reasoning correctly supports the individual number, whether it enables traceability to the source, and whether it hallucinates or lacks explanation.
